newsitem.title: USA: Colgate-Palmolive posts record sales, profits.
newsitem.headline: Colgate-Palmolive posts record sales, profits.

text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co. said Thursday that it posted record sales and profits in the third quarter as all its divisions contributed to strong volume growth in sales around the world.

The consumer products giant reported net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 of $160.9 million, or $1.06 a share, after posting a loss of $250.4 million, or $1.76 a share, a year ago, when it took a $460.5 million charge.
The per-share earnings were a penny better than Wall Street expectations of $1.05 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Without the charge for restructuring last year, the New York-based company would have posted a profit of $119 million, or 78 cents a share.
Colgate-Palmolive, which makes a variety of personal care and household products, said its sales in the quarter expanded to $2.2 billion from $2.13 billion, with all geographical areas posting gains.

"We are delighted with these strong results, especially since the excellent growth in sales and profits was well balanced between developed and developing regions of the world," Chairman Reuben Mark said in a statement.
"Volume growth in the developing world was strong, but we are particularly encouraged with the excellent shipment increases in our North American and European businesses," he added.

Colgate said its sales volume grew by 5 percent in North America, helped by the introduction of 11 new products in the United States. Sales volume expanded by 4 percent in Europe, where the company increased its market share for several products, notably toothpaste.
Dollar sales in Europe were flat, however, due to the strengthening of the dollar against other currencies.

Colgate-Palmolive said sales volume grew by 8 percent in Latin America, where it also introduced a number of new products, primarily soaps, bleaches and detergents. Results were especially good in Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador, Brazil and Mexico, the company said.
The company's Asia-Africa division also boosted its sales volume by 5 percent as it introduced new products, especially shampoo and dishwashing soaps.
Colgate-Palmolive's stock added $1 to $89.875 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange,
